avatar._note: Edenvia sells one product to MANY avatars, one per angle. Each angle has a full sheet in edenvia/avatars/*.md. This block is the DEFAULT angle A8 only; every spec names its angle and takes the avatar from that angle's sheet (edenvia/avatars/lymphatic-bloating.md).
avatar.who: a woman 35–55 (40s on screen) with persistently swollen, heavy, tender legs, sometimes arms, who has dieted and exercised for years because she believed it was ordinary fat; soft build, legs she hides, tired after standing. Never a young fitness model.
avatar.core_problem: swollen, heavy, puffy legs that never responded to dieting — 'it's not a fat problem'
secondary_problems: bloated, puffy belly and face in the morning
heaviness and aching after standing all day
dismissed by doctors and told to just lose weight
the wardrobe organised around hiding her legs
hides_it_by: long skirts, wide trousers, never shorts
sitting with her legs tucked away, out of photos
blaming her discipline, dieting even harder
already_tried: compression, dry brushing, diuretic teas, generic 'water pills'
avatar.pleasure_he_keeps: her meals, her coffee, her evenings — nothing to give up and nothing more to restrict: one tablet in a glass of water
proud_proof: ankles and calves visibly slimmer by evening
the boots zip up, the rings slide on
standing for hours without the heavy, aching legs
shorts in summer, legs in the photo

mechanism: plain words: when the body can't clear everyday oxidative stress, the tissue in the legs stays inflamed and stops draining normally, so fluid sits there — heavy, tender, puffy — and no diet reaches it, because it was never fat. The tablet turns a glass of water into hydrogen-rich water; hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is, reaches the tissue, and helps the body switch that process off so normal drainage can resume. Structure/function wording only ('helps support', 'helps your body'). Jargon never printed: microvascular, lymphatic dysfunction (as a diagnosis), lipedema/lip edema, lymphedema, redox, selective antioxidant, hydroxyl radical, ROS, NSAID, bioavailability. Allowed because the brand prints them: inflammation, inflammatory response, oxidative stress, cellular, 8PPM, lymphatic (as 'lymphatic drainage support').

compliance: Structure/function claims only: 'supports', 'helps maintain', 'may support', 'helps your body…'. Never diagnose, treat, cure, prevent, reverse, heal, manage a condition (DSHEA rollout doc, 2026-09-21).

Never name a disease or medical condition in headline or body. 'Inflammation', 'oxidative stress', 'stiff joints', 'afternoon crash', 'stubborn numbers' are allowed; 'arthritis', 'hypertension', 'diabetes', 'fatty liver' are not.
No invented NAMED doctors or celebrities. 'Trusted by healthcare professionals' is allowed (founder, 2026-10-11).
No fake testimonials as real; no stat without a real source and its footnote (B16).
No body before/after presented as a real customer.
Never say it replaces a medication or that someone should stop one.

Disclaimer (short DSHEA version), only where the template has the slot: 'These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.'
Tone: the founder wants VERY AGGRESSIVE ads (2026-10-11). Aggressive on the pain, the enemy belief and the offer; never aggressive on a disease claim.
'*Results may vary' footnote allowed wherever the template carries one (follow the swipe file).
Age callouts ('after 40', 'over 50') allowed when the template carries one (follow the swipe file).

The swipe-file brands (Metabolae, Lirae) print A1C, insulin, diabetes, metformin, dialysis. Edenvia clones the template, not the disease claim: every such line is rewritten to structure/function before the spec passes lint.
